Goal: Use all predictors, and measure classification quality using accuracy and F1 Score (balanced reporting for both classes).


```{python}
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split, GridSearchCV, cross_val_score
from sklearn.metrics import (
    confusion_matrix, classification_report, accuracy_score,
    f1_score
)
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler
from sklearn.pipeline import Pipeline
from sklearn.impute import SimpleImputer

from sklearn.discriminant_analysis import LinearDiscriminantAnalysis, QuadraticDiscriminantAnalysis
from sklearn.svm import SVC
from sklearn.tree import DecisionTreeClassifier
from sklearn.neighbors import KNeighborsClassifier
from sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression

from plotnine import ggplot, aes, geom_point, theme_minimal, labs

# Load full data
url = "https://www.dropbox.com/s/s2a1uoiegitupjc/cannabis_full.csv?dl=1"
canna = pd.read_csv(url)

# Drop non‑numeric predictors, keep Type as target
non_num_cols = ["Strain", "Effects", "Flavor"]
canna_num = canna.drop(columns=non_num_cols)

# Binary subset: indica vs sativa
# different name for binary dataset
binary = canna_num[canna_num["Type"].isin(["indica", "sativa"])].copy() # use isin()
Xb = binary.drop(columns=["Type"])
yb = binary["Type"]

Xb_train, Xb_test, yb_train, yb_test = train_test_split(
    Xb, yb, test_size=0.3, random_state=123, stratify=yb
)

```

Accuracy is suitable when classes are reasonably balanced and overall correct classifications are the main concern. Macro-averaged F1 score is selected for model comparisons, as it balances performance across all classes, especially when class sizes or classification difficulty vary. F1 evaluates both precision and recall, and macro averaging ensures no single class is prioritized over others.



```{python}
def report_results(name, y_true, y_pred):
    print(f"=== {name} ===")
    print("Accuracy:", accuracy_score(y_true, y_pred))
    print("Macro F1:", f1_score(y_true, y_pred, average="macro"))
    print("Confusion matrix:\n", confusion_matrix(y_true, y_pred))

```

# Part One – Binary (indica vs sativa)

```{python}
lda_pipe = Pipeline([
    ("imputer", SimpleImputer(strategy="most_frequent")),
    ("scaler", StandardScaler(with_mean=False)),
    ("lda", LinearDiscriminantAnalysis())
])

lda_param_grid = {
    "lda__solver": ["svd", "lsqr"] # what are these hyperparameter? 
}
# use grid? =-==
lda_grid = GridSearchCV(
    lda_pipe,
    lda_param_grid,
    cv=5,
    scoring="f1_macro",
    n_jobs=-1
)

# fitting the model
lda_grid.fit(Xb_train, yb_train)
# extracting the best scores 
print("Best CV macro F1 (LDA):", lda_grid.best_score_) #.best_score_ 
print("Best params:", lda_grid.best_params_) # .best_params_

best_lda = lda_grid.best_estimator_
yb_pred_lda = best_lda.predict(Xb_test)
report_results("LDA (binary)", yb_test, yb_pred_lda)

```

**Interpretation**:
LDA performed well on binary classification, achieving high accuracy and balanced F1 score. The confusion matrix shows more errors in predicting sativa strains—42 indica samples were misclassified as sativa, while only 15 sativa samples were misclassified as indica. This may be due to more overlap or shared effects between these classes. Most predictions were correct, indicating that the features effectively separate indica and sativa strains.

## Q2: QDA


```{python}

qda_pipe = Pipeline([
    ("imputer", SimpleImputer(strategy="most_frequent")),  # or "median"
    ("scaler", StandardScaler(with_mean=False)),
    ("qda", QuadraticDiscriminantAnalysis())
])

qda_param_grid = {
    "qda__reg_param": [0.0, 0.001, 0.01, 0.1, 0.5]
}

qda_grid = GridSearchCV(
    qda_pipe,
    qda_param_grid,
    cv=5,
    scoring="f1_macro",
    n_jobs=-1
)

qda_grid.fit(Xb_train, yb_train)

print("Best CV macro F1 (QDA):", qda_grid.best_score_)
print("Best params:", qda_grid.best_params_)

best_qda = qda_grid.best_estimator_
yb_pred_qda = best_qda.predict(Xb_test)
report_results("QDA (binary)", yb_test, yb_pred_qda)
# warning shows : this is not a fatal error—just a diagnostic about multicollinearity
```

**Interpretation**:
QDA shows slightly lower performance compared to LDA, with more misclassifications overall. The warning about covariance matrix collinearity highlights redundancy in feature dummies, which can affect QDA accuracy. Errors are again more frequent for sativa misclassified as indica.
## Q3: SVC (linear)

```{python}
svc_lin_pipe = Pipeline([
    ("imputer", SimpleImputer(strategy="most_frequent")),
    ("scaler", StandardScaler()),
    ("svc", SVC(kernel="linear"))
])

svc_lin_param_grid = {
    "svc__C": [0.01, 0.1, 1, 10]
}

svc_lin_grid = GridSearchCV(
    svc_lin_pipe,
    svc_lin_param_grid,
    cv=5,
    scoring="f1_macro",
    n_jobs=-1
)

svc_lin_grid.fit(Xb_train, yb_train)

print("Best CV macro F1 (SVC linear):", svc_lin_grid.best_score_)
print("Best params:", svc_lin_grid.best_params_)

best_svc_lin = svc_lin_grid.best_estimator_
yb_pred_svc_lin = best_svc_lin.predict(Xb_test)
report_results("SVC linear (binary)", yb_test, yb_pred_svc_lin)

```

**Interpretation**:
SVC with a linear kernel yields slightly higher accuracy than LDA and QDA. The confusion pattern is similar: sativa strains are misidentified more often than indica strains. Overall, the linear decision boundary fits these data well.


## Q4: SVM (polynomial kernel)


```{python}

# Using the numeric-only version of the data
X = canna_num.drop(columns=["Type"])
y = canna_num["Type"]

X_train, X_test, y_train, y_test = train_test_split(
    X, y, test_size=0.3, random_state=123, stratify=y
)

# created the splut again, didnt use from the last one

svm_poly_pipe = Pipeline([
    ("imputer", SimpleImputer(strategy="most_frequent")),
    ("scaler", StandardScaler()),
    ("svm", SVC(kernel="poly"))
])

svm_poly_param_grid = {
    "svm__C": [0.1, 1, 10],
    "svm__degree": [2, 3, 4],
    "svm__gamma": ["scale", "auto"]
}

svm_poly_grid = GridSearchCV(
    svm_poly_pipe,
    svm_poly_param_grid,
    cv=5,
    scoring="f1_macro",
    n_jobs=-1
)

svm_poly_grid.fit(Xb_train, yb_train)

print("Best CV macro F1 (SVM poly):", svm_poly_grid.best_score_)
print("Best params:", svm_poly_grid.best_params_)

best_svm_poly = svm_poly_grid.best_estimator_
yb_pred_svm_poly = best_svm_poly.predict(Xb_test)
report_results("SVM poly (binary)", yb_test, yb_pred_svm_poly)

```

**Interpretation**:
The polynomial-kernel SVM model performs similarly to the linear SVC, with comparable accuracy and confusion structure. There is not a substantial gain in macro F1 or accuracy from using a polynomial kernel here, suggesting that the boundary between indica and sativa is mostly linear.


# Part Two – Natural multiclass

## Q1: Decision tree, plot and interpret


```{python}
tree = DecisionTreeClassifier(random_state=123)

tree_param_grid = {
    "max_depth": [3, 5, 8, None],
    "min_samples_leaf": [1, 5, 10]
}

tree_grid = GridSearchCV(
    tree,
    tree_param_grid,
    cv=5,
    scoring="f1_macro",
    n_jobs=-1
)

tree_grid.fit(X_train, y_train)

print("Best CV macro F1 (Tree):", tree_grid.best_score_)
print("Best params:", tree_grid.best_params_)

best_tree = tree_grid.best_estimator_
y_pred_tree = best_tree.predict(X_test)
report_results("Decision Tree (multiclass)", y_test, y_pred_tree)

```
Top features: Sleepy, Energetic

**Interpretation**:
The tree achieves lower accuracy and macro F1 compared to binary tasks. Sleepy and Energetic are the most important features distinguishing classes. The matrix shows that hybrid samples are especially likely to be misclassified as indica or sativa, confirming that hybrids share properties and are harder to separate.

## Q3 (comparison)

Metrics in multiclass tasks are notably worse than in binary classification. This is mainly due to increased decision complexity: hybrids combine features of both other classes, leading to greater overlaps and more misclassifications. The confusion matrices consistently show that hybrid strains are the most likely to be misclassified, typically as indica or sativa. This demonstrates that hybrids are less distinct in feature space and their properties are distributed between the other types.


# Part Three – Multiclass from Binary

```{python}
def make_binary_target(y, positive_label):
    return (y == positive_label).astype(int)

```

## Q1: OvR – Logistic Regression and SVC

```{python}
ovr_results = []

for cls in ["indica", "sativa", "hybrid"]:
    # Binary targets: class vs rest
    y_train_bin = make_binary_target(y_train, cls)
    y_test_bin = make_binary_target(y_test, cls)

    # Logistic Regression OvR
    lr_pipe = Pipeline([
        ("imputer", SimpleImputer(strategy="most_frequent")),
        ("scaler", StandardScaler()),
        ("logreg", LogisticRegression(max_iter=1000))
    ])

    lr_grid = GridSearchCV(
        lr_pipe,
        {"logreg__C": [0.1, 1, 10]},
        cv=5,
        scoring="f1",
        n_jobs=-1
    )
    lr_grid.fit(X_train, y_train_bin)
    best_lr = lr_grid.best_estimator_
    y_pred_lr = best_lr.predict(X_test)
    f1_lr = f1_score(y_test_bin, y_pred_lr)

    print(f"\nLogReg OvR: {cls} vs rest")
    print("Best CV F1:", lr_grid.best_score_)
    report_results(f"LogReg OvR {cls}", y_test_bin, y_pred_lr)

    ovr_results.append(("LogReg", cls, lr_grid.best_score_, f1_lr))

    # SVC OvR (linear kernel)
    svc_pipe = Pipeline([
        ("imputer", SimpleImputer(strategy="most_frequent")),
        ("scaler", StandardScaler()),
        ("svc", SVC(kernel="linear"))
    ])

    svc_grid = GridSearchCV(
        svc_pipe,
        {"svc__C": [0.1, 1, 10]},
        cv=5,
        scoring="f1",
        n_jobs=-1
    )
    svc_grid.fit(X_train, y_train_bin)
    best_svc = svc_grid.best_estimator_
    y_pred_svc = best_svc.predict(X_test)
    f1_svc = f1_score(y_test_bin, y_pred_svc)

    print(f"\nSVC OvR: {cls} vs rest")
    print("Best CV F1:", svc_grid.best_score_)
    report_results(f"SVC OvR {cls}", y_test_bin, y_pred_svc)

    ovr_results.append(("SVC", cls, svc_grid.best_score_, f1_svc))

ovr_results_df = pd.DataFrame(
    ovr_results,
    columns=["Model", "Positive_class", "CV_F1", "Test_F1"]
)
ovr_results_df
```
**Interpretation**:
The OvR models do best at distinguishing hybrids from non-hybrids, likely because hybrid strains include distinct effects not present in only indica/sativa. Models are worst at pulling out sativa strains alone, likely due to the overlap in features with indica and hybrids.
Use ovo_results_df to answer Q4 (which pair/model is easiest/hardest, does this make sense).

## Q3: OvO – Logistic Regression and SVC


```{python}
pairs = [("indica", "sativa"),
         ("indica", "hybrid"),
         ("hybrid", "sativa")]

ovo_results = []

for c1, c2 in pairs:
    # Subset data to just the two classes
    mask_train = y_train.isin([c1, c2])
    mask_test = y_test.isin([c1, c2])

    X_pair_train = X_train[mask_train]
    y_pair_train = y_train[mask_train]
    X_pair_test = X_test[mask_test]
    y_pair_test = y_test[mask_test]

    # Logistic Regression
    lr_pipe = Pipeline([
        ("imputer", SimpleImputer(strategy="most_frequent")),
        ("scaler", StandardScaler()),
        ("logreg", LogisticRegression(max_iter=1000))
    ])

    lr_grid = GridSearchCV(
        lr_pipe,
        {"logreg__C": [0.1, 1, 10]},
        cv=5,
        scoring="f1_macro",
        n_jobs=-1
    )
    lr_grid.fit(X_pair_train, y_pair_train)
    best_lr = lr_grid.best_estimator_
    y_pred_lr = best_lr.predict(X_pair_test)

    print(f"\nLogReg OvO: {c1} vs {c2}")
    print("Best CV macro F1:", lr_grid.best_score_)
    report_results(f"LogReg OvO {c1} vs {c2}", y_pair_test, y_pred_lr)

    ovo_results.append(
        ("LogReg", f"{c1} vs {c2}", lr_grid.best_score_,
         f1_score(y_pair_test, y_pred_lr, average="macro"))
    )

    # SVC (linear)
    svc_pipe = Pipeline([
        ("imputer", SimpleImputer(strategy="most_frequent")),
        ("scaler", StandardScaler()),
        ("svc", SVC(kernel="linear"))
    ])

    svc_grid = GridSearchCV(
        svc_pipe,
        {"svc__C": [0.1, 1, 10]},
        cv=5,
        scoring="f1_macro",
        n_jobs=-1
    )
    svc_grid.fit(X_pair_train, y_pair_train)
    best_svc = svc_grid.best_estimator_
    y_pred_svc = best_svc.predict(X_pair_test)

    print(f"\nSVC OvO: {c1} vs {c2}")
    print("Best CV macro F1:", svc_grid.best_score_)
    report_results(f"SVC OvO {c1} vs {c2}", y_pair_test, y_pred_svc)

    ovo_results.append(
        ("SVC", f"{c1} vs {c2}", svc_grid.best_score_,
         f1_score(y_pair_test, y_pred_svc, average="macro"))
    )

ovo_results_df = pd.DataFrame(
    ovo_results,
    columns=["Model", "Pair", "CV_F1_macro", "Test_F1_macro"]
)
ovo_results_df

```


**Interpretation**:
Binary classification between indica and sativa remains the most accurate and balanced. Hybrid-related pairs are consistently hardest, with confusion matrices showing hybrids are mispredicted as sativa (and vice versa) more often than other pairs. This confirms hybrids have overlapping feature sets and are not strongly defined by any single effect or flavor word.



## Q5: Documentation question 

In sklearn, LogisticRegression uses a one-vs-rest (OvR) strategy by default for multiclass data


In sklearn, SVC uses a one-vs-one (OvO) strategy automatically for multiclass input.
